topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This topic covers the lecturer's opening remarks, course context, and the primary learning objectives for the lecture.

topics.label: Multifactorial drivers, environmental factors, and epidemiology of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the general concepts of cancer etiology, contrasting endogenous processes, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures through statistical debate and global epidemiological data.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and viral oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on biological agents—including viruses, bacteria, and parasites—and the specific infectious etiology and chromosomal translocations of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Dietary aflatoxin and metabolic DNA adduct formation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic specifically examines the dietary fungal toxin aflatoxin and its oxidative conversion in the liver into reactive DNA-binding adducts.

topics.label: Ultraviolet radiation and thymine dimer DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic addresses physical radiation damage to DNA via ultraviolet light and the resulting formation of pyrimidine dimers.

topics.label: Chemical carcinogens, xenobiotic metabolism, and tissue-specific activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine chemical carcinogens—including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, dioxins, and aromatic amines—and their processing by xenobiotic metabolic pathways in host tissues.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and the two-stage carcinogenesis model
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, focusing on chronic inflammatory microenvironments and the classic two-stage initiator-promoter paradigm.

topics.label: Developmental and life-stage susceptibility to carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how host developmental timing, age, and reproductive life stages modulate tissue vulnerability to carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Mutational signatures and genomic profiling of carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details high-throughput genomic sequencing techniques used to identify characteristic mutational patterns left by specific carcinogens.

topics.label: Epidemiological cohort studies and population biobanks
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic covers human population-level methodologies, urinary biomarker tracking, and large-scale biobank resources used to establish carcinogenic associations.

topics.label: In vivo rodent carcinogenicity bioassays
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines whole-animal toxicology studies in rodents to test compound carcinogenicity, along with the limitations and dosage challenges of animal models.

topics.label: In vitro bacterial mutagenesis testing and risk-benefit evaluation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the in vitro Ames test using bacterial cultures and metabolizing extracts, concluding with the broader societal evaluation of exposure risks versus benefits.
